blindSummary:
Three trans women were murdered in less than a week in July 2024 (one disappeared and found dead days later; one killed while sex working); four transfeminicides recorded in July 2024 alone and five for the year in the national NGO yearbook - second only to the country's capital. Activists reported six trans women killed in a short period and accused three levels of government of rights omissions. This state/province's penal code contains no transfeminicide offence, and its 2019 hate-crime provision covers sexual orientation but not gender identity - meaning a visitor assaulted in the state's largest city faces a legal framework with no specific protective category. There is an anti-conversion-practices law carrying 2-5 years, and the national observatory's verdict on such statutes is that transfeminicide 'advances in law but not in sentences.'

Legislative response has been refusal: an initiative filed by a trans collective was 'ignored and finally lapsed,' prompting a 50+-day protest encampment outside the congress of this state/province still ongoing in January 2026 (activists report harassment and lack of basic facilities at the camp). A deputy of a small national party in 2026 could only ask the congress to 'unfreeze' the bill. There is no investigative unit, no protocol, and no named offence to invoke. The gap between nominal coverage and protection is documented in the observatory review 'transfeminicide advances in law but not in sentences.'

For context elsewhere: the country's capital pairs a similar lethality record with a dedicated transfeminicide investigation unit (Dec 2024), mandatory-response protocols and a gender police force (Aug 2025); a coastal state was the first in the country to typify the crime (March 2024). This state/province's explicit legislative refusal is the opposite signal.
blindSourceSummaries: LGBTI+ news agency report (31 Jul 2024): three transfeminicides in this state/province in under a week - a 23-year-old trans woman disappeared on 7 July and found dead on 29 July; a second killed on 30 July during sex work; a third killed in a motel, reported 27 June. The state prosecutor's office had issued no information on any case; local activists demand gender-perspective investigation protocols. The article notes at least 36 transfeminicides nationally in 2024 per a national assembly of trans and non-binary people, and at least four trans women killed in the state that year.

The country's longest-running civil-society hate-crime observatory (active since 1998) yearbook (May 2025), on hate-motivated homicides: records the capital as the state with the most LGBT+ killings in 2024 (17 homicides, 11 trans women), ahead of this state/province (5); notes the country has no official registry of bias-motivated violence, and documents under-counting where media accounts lack victim names and gender data.

A fact-checking outlet investigation (9 Aug 2024): the three killings in a week in this state/province against a state that 'lacks measures to sanction transfeminicide.' Cites the national hate-crime observatory: 51 hate crimes (forced disappearances or murders) against LGBTIQ+ people January-July 2024 nationally, trans women 56.86% of victims; in the state itself 7 aggressions against trans women in 2024 - 3 forced disappearances and 4 transfeminicides.

Local news outlet report (12 Jan 2026): a trans collective keeps its protest camp outside the congress of this state/province past 50 days, vowing to stay until transfeminicide is typified in the penal code; an earlier initiative sat unanswered for a year in the official state filing office and lapsed. A co-founder describes harassment at the camp, missing basic facilities, roughly 50 trans deaths/disappearances among her acquaintances over 35 years, and 16 trans community deaths counted informally from 2024 into early 2025 but not registered because of misclassification.
blindTangential: The July 2024 killings cluster and the lapsed bill are transfeminicide-specific, but the broader 2024 record (51 hate crimes nationally, 56.86% trans women) shows a general hostility climate toward LGBT+ people that a non-trans gender-nonconforming visitor could also meet.
blindLocalsOnly: Conversion-practice criminalisation (2-5 years) on the books but unenforced, and the absence of an administrative gender-recognition procedure, are resident-facing gaps.
